introduction: “Be united, O peoples of the earth!” The guide begins with the summons and immediately turns it on the believers themselves, who are told in letter after letter that they are quarrelling, that discord has been the cause of every weakness, and that the sufferings of the Founder were borne for nothing else than their unity; only then does it widen to the removal of prejudice and war. Paul wrote such letters to Corinth and Galatia; the Qur’an tells believers to hold together to one cable and to make peace between parties; Jesus asks that his friends be one “that the world may believe”; Proverbs counts the sower of discord among the things God hates. But unity has been doubted by serious people, and by scripture. Jesus says he brings a sword; Paul withstood Peter to his face and parted from Barnabas; Jeremiah denounces those who cry “Peace, peace” where there is none; Kant, Madison, Milton and Blake each hold that conflict, faction or contraries do work that concord cannot.
questions: Jesus prays “that they all may be one; that the world may believe”. Why do the readings make the unity of the believers the condition of their service to everyone else (readings 5 and 6)?
Paul withstood Peter to the face, and reading 15 says no one should object to another. How can a community be both honest and undivided?
Jeremiah condemns those who say “Peace, peace; when there is no peace.” What would false unity look like in a community, and which readings guard against it?

Kant says nature wills discord, Madison that faction is sown in human nature, Blake that without contraries there is no progression. What exactly do the readings mean by discord, and is it what these three defend?
Readings 36 to 38 name prejudice and irreverence toward others’ leaders as causes of strife. Why might reverent speech about another community’s founders do more than agreements?

outside.why: “Be united, O peoples of the earth!” The Qur’an: hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of God, and do not separate.
Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
A hundred thousand blessings on the soul that unifies hearts. Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
“Make not God’s religion a cause of dissension.” The Qur’an to its Prophet: as for those who sunder their religion and become schismatics, no concern at all hast thou with them.

Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. Jesus expects his message to divide households. Is division sometimes the mark of a true word and not its abuse?
What flourishes springs from fellowship, what lies in ruin from enmity. If a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

Kant thought otherwise about how things flourish: man wills concord, but nature knows better what is good for his species; she wills discord, and so draws out his powers. What would the reading answer?
Believers must first be in harmony themselves before they can heal others. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
“The most pressing need today is harmony and union among the friends.” That they all may be one; that the world may believe.
Strive night and day to remove conflict among the peoples. If two parties of believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them.
“We have commanded … unity and harmony, yet still” there is discord. Paul to Corinth: every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos. Is Christ divided?
“The friends are quarreling.” If ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another.
James on the root of quarrels among believers: ye lust, and have not; ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.
That all “may become as one soul”. The multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul.
Strive for concord with everyone you meet. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.
Union, love and uprightness. Above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.
Avoid whatever causes the least discord. With all lowliness and meekness, forbearing one another in love; endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
“No one should interfere with or object to another.” Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth.
Paul tells how at Antioch he withstood Peter to the face, because he was to be blamed. The churches kept that story. When is objection a service to unity?
Allow no opening “even as small as a hair’s breadth”. The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.
Those adorned with recognition must remove differences. Leave there thy gift before the altar; first be reconciled to thy brother.
“Spread not corruption in the earth … hold fast unto unity.” Of the things the Lord hates, the last named is he that soweth discord among brethren.
“The cause of weakness … hath been discord.” The Qur’an: dispute not one with another lest ye falter and your strength depart from you.
Aesop’s father hands his sons a bundle of sticks they cannot break, then the sticks one by one.
Until they become as one being they will be scattered. A threefold cord is not quickly broken.
“You can remove this cloudiness and establish love.” Abram to Lot: let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee; for we be brethren.

If affection is not established, separation follows. Paul and Barnabas, after a sharp contention over a companion, departed asunder one from the other, and the work went on in two directions. Is every separation a defeat?
In all ages discord has been the cause of abasement. Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation.
The purpose of bearing these tribulations is that souls should walk in unity. He is our peace, who hath broken down the middle wall of partition.
Were all the trials of Bahá’u’lláh and the martyrs without result? Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
Become as one soul and one spirit. Whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all rejoice.
You are “the cause of fellowship”. The Prophet’s likeness of the believers in their mutual love: one body; when one limb aches, the whole body answers with wakefulness and fever.
The unity of the Word among the faithful. That ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; perfectly joined together in the same mind.

Milton welcomed the many opinions of a people in earnest: opinion in good men is but knowledge in the making; a little generous prudence, a little forbearance of one another, might join all these diligences. Does unity of the Word require the same mind on every question?
Their unity is to gather the conflicting peoples. Then will I turn to the people a pure language, to serve him with one consent.
The Gardener prunes and weeds. Every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.
Remove racial, patriotic and religious prejudice. Have not the faith with respect of persons.
“Strife and animosity are due to misunderstandings.” Montaigne: there is more ado to interpret interpretations than to interpret things.

Madison held that the causes of faction are sown in the nature of man, and that the remedy is to control its effects, not to remove its causes. The readings propose to remove the causes. Which is the realist?
Peace will come when people “mention each other’s leaders with due reverence”. The Qur’an: revile not those unto whom they pray beside God, lest they wrongfully revile God through ignorance.
He brought fellowship among contending denominations. At Pentecost men of every nation heard the same speech, each in his own tongue.
Had Christ’s principles of unity remained in hearts, men would have refrained from war. Put up again thy sword into his place.
Become the dawning-place of this brotherhood. All within the four seas will be his brothers.
“Our origin has been one and our end must be” one. Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?

“We seek peace and harmony and consistently call for unity.” Jeremiah warns of leaders who heal the hurt of the people slightly, saying Peace, peace; when there is no peace. What distinguishes the call to unity from that?
That East and West may embrace. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
Tagore’s prayer for his country: where the world has not been broken up into fragments by narrow domestic walls.
“We spread the carpet of fellowship.” The psalmist among those who hate peace: I am for peace: but when I speak, they are for war.
The primary divine purpose is the unity of humankind. No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main.
This century is to reveal the light of unity. Tennyson dreamed it in 1842: the Parliament of man, the Federation of the world.
That the causes of discord be eliminated and the light of unity illumine hearts. It is in the minds of men that the defences of peace must be constructed.
“From time immemorial hath the True One summoned the people unto unity.” Micah’s vision: every man under his vine and under his fig tree, and none shall make them afraid.
“Victory through unity.” Blake: without contraries is no progression. Does the unity of the readings have room for contraries, and where?
Whoever promotes concord is recorded in God’s Book. The fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.
From a collective body “another effect becomes manifest”. We, being many, are one body, and every one members one of another.

shortfall: Many of the readings repeat a single command, to hold fast to unity and avoid discord, in nearly the same words; companions were given to its distinct forms and reasons and not to each repetition.
